questions.q: What does a function declaration (prototype) specify?
choices: The function's name, return type, and parameter list (number and types of parameters)
The code that runs when the function is called
Only the function's name
The function's name and the values of its arguments
questions.explain: A prototype gives only type information: name, return type, and parameter list. The definition is the part that contains the body.

questions.q: In C, every function must be declared before it is called.
questions.explain: You can do this with a prototype or by putting the full definition before the call.

questions.q: main is defined near the top of a file and calls max, whose definition comes after main. Which of these would satisfy C's rule that a function is declared before it is called?
choices: Put the prototype int max(int n1, int n2); above main
Move the full definition of max above main
Put the prototype int max(int n1, int n2); after main
Nothing; C finds the definition anywhere in the file automatically
questions.explain: The function has to be declared before the call, either with a prototype or with the full definition placed earlier in the file.

questions.q: Which is a correctly written prototype for a function named average that takes two int parameters a and b and returns a double?
choices: double average(int a, int b);
average(int a, int b) double;
double average(int a, b);
double average(int a; int b);
questions.explain: The format is <return type> <name>(<type> <param>, <type> <param>). Every parameter needs its own type, and parameters are separated by commas.

questions.q: Which return type should a C function use if it does not return a value?
questions.explain: Functions that don't return a value use the void return type, like print_table.

questions.q: A C function can return several values of different types with a single return statement.
questions.explain: A C function returns a single value of a specific type: its declared return type.

questions.q: According to the recommended style for function comments, what should a function's comment describe?
choices: What the function does
Each parameter: what it's used for and what should be passed
What the function returns
The memory address of each parameter
questions.explain: The example comments (such as the one for max) describe the function's purpose, each parameter, and the return value.

questions.q: Every C program must have a main function.
questions.explain: main defines what the program does when it begins executing and usually organizes the program's big-picture behavior.

questions.q: When you call a C function, how many arguments do you pass?
choices: One argument for each of the function's parameters
As many as you like; extra arguments are ignored
Always exactly one
Zero; parameters get their values from global variables
questions.explain: Each function parameter gets one corresponding argument.

questions.q: An argument in a function call can be an expression such as val1 * 2, not just a variable name or a literal.
questions.explain: The argument list is a list of expressions. In max(val1 * 2, val2), the expression is evaluated and its value (12 when val1 is 6) is passed.

questions.q: max(x, y) returns the larger of its two int arguments. If val1 = 6 and val2 = 10, what does max(val1 * 2, val2) return?
questions.explain: The arguments are 12 and 10, so max returns 12.

questions.q: print_table(int start, int stop) runs for (i = start; i <= stop; i++) and prints i*i on each iteration. How many values does print_table(6, 10) print?
questions.explain: i takes the values 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. The loop condition is <=, so both ends are included.

questions.q: print_table(int start, int stop) prints i*i for i from start to stop inclusive, separated by tabs. What does print_table(3, 5) print?
questions.explain: It prints the squares of 3, 4, and 5: 9, 16, 25.

questions.q: max returns an int. Which statement uses max's return value correctly, given int val1, val2, result;?
choices: result = max(val1, val2);
max(val1, val2) = result;
result = max;
max(result) = val1, val2;
questions.explain: Call the function by name with its argument list, then assign the returned int to a variable.

questions.q: What does it mean that C passes arguments by value?
choices: Each parameter is assigned the value of its corresponding argument, so assigning a new value to a parameter inside the function is not visible to the caller
The parameter and the caller's argument variable are the same storage, so changes to the parameter change the caller's variable
Only literal values (like 5) can be passed, not variables
The function's return value is copied into every argument variable
questions.explain: Each parameter receives the argument's value. Changing the parameter affects only the function's own copy.

questions.q: If a C function assigns a new value to one of its int parameters, the variable the caller passed as the argument also changes.
questions.explain: Under pass by value, the caller does not see changes to a parameter.
bump gets a copy of a's value. Incrementing n inside bump does not change a in main.
y (100) > x (13), so x is set to 100 inside max before the printf.

questions.q: Same modified max as above (it does x = y when y > x). main runs res = max(a, b); with a = 13 and b = 100. After the call returns, what is the value of a in main?
questions.explain: x only holds a copy of a's value. Assigning to x inside max does not change a.

questions.q: A version of max that runs x = y on its parameter when y > x returns the same result and leaves the caller's variables the same as a version without that statement.
questions.explain: Arguments are passed by value, so the extra assignment only changes max's local copy. The two versions behave the same from the caller's point of view.

questions.q: What does a stack frame contain?
choices: The parameter and local variable values for one function call
The compiled machine code of every function in the program
Only the function's return value
All global variables in the program
questions.explain: Each function call creates a new stack frame that holds that call's parameters and local variables.

questions.q: A stack frame is also called an activation ______ (give either accepted word).
questions.explain: A stack frame is also called an activation frame or an activation record.

questions.q: What happens on the execution stack when a function is called?
choices: A new stack frame for the function is pushed on top of the stack, with space for its parameters and local variables
The caller's stack frame is removed and replaced by the new function's frame
A new frame is added at the bottom of the stack
Nothing; stack frames are only created when a function returns
questions.explain: Calling a function pushes a new frame on top. The caller's frame stays underneath it.

questions.q: What happens on the execution stack when a function returns?
choices: Its stack frame is popped off the top, leaving the caller's frame on top
Its stack frame stays on the stack until the program ends
All frames on the stack are removed
The caller's frame is popped, and the returning function's frame becomes active
questions.explain: Returning pops the function's frame, so the caller's frame is the active (top) frame again.

questions.q: Only the local variables and parameters in the top (active) stack frame are in scope.
questions.explain: The top frame belongs to the function activation that is currently running. Only its locals and parameters are in scope.

questions.q: main calls max and nothing else is running. While max is executing, how many stack frames are on the execution stack?
questions.explain: main's frame is at the bottom and max's frame is on top of it.

questions.q: main declares int a, b, res; and calls res = max(a, b);. max is defined as int max(int x, int y) and declares a local int bigger. Just before max executes its return statement, which variables are in max's stack frame?
choices: x
y
bigger
a
res
questions.explain: max's frame holds its parameters (x, y) and its local (bigger). a, b, and res are in main's frame.

questions.q: main declares int a, b, res; and runs res = max(a, b); with a = 11 and b = 7. Just before max executes its return statement, what is stored in res in main's stack frame?
choices: Nothing meaningful yet (undefined), because max hasn't returned and the assignment hasn't happened
0, because local variables always start at zero
questions.explain: res is assigned only after max returns. Until then it has no defined value.

questions.q: main runs res = max(a, b); with a = 11 and b = 7, using the original max (no x = y statement). Just before max returns, which of these are true?
choices: x in max's frame is 11
y in max's frame is 7
bigger in max's frame is 11
a in main's frame is 7
questions.explain: x and y get copies of a (11) and b (7). bigger is 11 because y is not greater than x. a is still 11.
